To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the myocardial collagen network is a dynamic, heterogeneous, and complex structure, the behaviour of which is determined by the balance between collagen synthesis and degradation.

1) the cardiac collagen network is a dynamic structure that is continuously remodelling in the adult heart and 2) in the hypertensive heart the collagen network undergoes an abnormal remodelling process that is responsible for the development of diastolic and systolic dysfunction.
myocardial collagen matrix remoulding is a major determinant of diastolic stiffness in hypertension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of collagen matrix remodellng in the myocardium of the spontaneously hypertensive rat (SHR).
the role of the interstitial matrix and the fibroblasts that produce it in the development of cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure.
the structural remodellng of the non-myocytes and the extracellular matrix of the myocardium in the spontaneously hypertensive rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

myocardial collagen remodelling, as it occurs in arterial hypertension, involves the following components: (a) increased synthesis and decreased degradation of collagen; (b) increased deposition of collagen; (c) increased collagen crosslinking and decreased turnover; (d) altered collagen composition; (e) increased collagen fibril formation; and (f) altered collagen fibril orientation.
the collagen matrix of the myocardium is an important determinant of the mechanical behaviour of the heart.
the collagen matrix is an important determinant of myocardial function in arterial hypertension, and that RAAS inhibition can prevent the development of myocardial fibrosis and its consequences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cardiac interstitium plays an important role in myocardial function, and that the structural remodellings that occur in arterial hypertension are mediated through the actions of the renin-angio- tensin-aldosterone system on the interstitial matrix and non-myocyte cells.

in hypertensive heart disease the myocardial collagen network is altered in structure, composition, and mechanical properties, which is the major determinant of the myocardial structural and functional abnormalities.

we have shown that cardiac fibroblats have a major role in mediating the adverse structural remodellng of the myocardium, and that the RAAS plays a central role in the development of myocardial interstitial fibrosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the collagen matrix of the heart plays a key role in the development of heart disease.
the cardiac fibroblast is a key regulator of myocardial structure, and that the fibrotic myocardium in hypertension is a dynamic entity.
cardiac fibroblats are the main players in cardiac remodeling and that their behavior is modulated by circulating and tissue RAS.
